metadata.title: TIMSS 2019 Assessment Frameworks: TIMSS & PIRLS
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center (Lynch School of Education, Boston College) / IEA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an assessment framework and does not provide an empirical analytic dataset, sampling frame, or weighting variables for student-level estimation. It describes TIMSS 2019 as an international assessment administered at fourth and eighth grades, with mathematics and science content organized by content and cognitive domains, and with additional context questionnaires. Because no microdata analysis is conducted here, complex survey weights (e.g., student/sampling weights and replicate weights) are not specified. For downstream analyses using TIMSS 2019 microdata, analysts should apply the official TIMSS sampling/analysis weights and replicate weights provided in the TIMSS international database to account for the multistage clustered design and to produce population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) and missing-data handling are not applicable in this framework volume because it does not estimate achievement models or train predictive/statistical models on TIMSS student microdata. The text focuses on defining assessment constructs (content/cognitive domains), questionnaire frameworks, and design considerations (including the transition to eTIMSS and PSI tasks), rather than reporting PV-based achievement results. Therefore, there is no PV generation/combination or missing-data procedure to document in this document.

data.outcome_summary: This volume documents the TIMSS 2019 assessment frameworks for mathematics and science (fourth and eighth grades) and the TIMSS 2019 context questionnaire framework, organizing the assessment around a content dimension (e.g., mathematics domains such as Number, Algebra, Geometry, Data and Probability; science domains such as Life/Physical/Earth Science and Biology/Chemistry/Physics) and a cognitive dimension (Knowing, Applying, Reasoning). It explains how the frameworks are updated iteratively using inputs from the TIMSS 2015 Encyclopedia, expert item review committees, and national research coordinators, ensuring coherence across assessment cycles. It also describes design considerations for eTIMSS, including the use of computer-based delivery for about half of participating countries and the introduction of PSIs (problem solving and inquiry tasks) that can generate process data about students’ approaches. The document further explains the rationale for a less difficult mathematics option at fourth grade (TIMSS Numeracy-linked items) to improve measurement at the lower end of the achievement scale and to support trend reporting on a common scale.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a framework/assessment-design publication rather than an empirical study. The provided text does not include an analytic sample, country-level student counts, PV estimation procedures, missing-data handling, or any ML model training/evaluation, so fields related to empirical outcomes and predictive performance are intentionally absent by design.
